title: Exercise 1: Titration of formic acid with a sodium hydroxide solution
body:
We want to model the titration of 20 mL of a formic acid solution (CA = 5.00⋅10−2 mol·L−1) by adding a sodium hydroxide solution (CB = 8.00⋅10−2 mol·L−1), according to the reaction: HCOOH(aq) + OH−(aq) ⇌ HCOO−(aq) + H2O(l)

Data: Acid dissociation constant of formic acid: KA = 10-3.75

Equilibrium constant for the autoionisation of water: KE = 10-14

A/ Plotting the titration curve and its derivative

Using numpy to create an ndarray

Instead of using a for loop, it is often simpler to use functions from the numpy module to create data arrays. Using numpy (usually abbreviated to np) lets you create N-dimensional arrays called ndarrays. Unlike standard Python lists, these arrays allow faster and more efficient data handling. However, working with them differs slightly from working with standard lists. For example, in a two-dimensional list or array, extracting the 4th element in the 3rd column is written in Python as:

x[3][2]

With numpy, this operation is written as:

x[3, 2]

Arrays can easily be generated using the following functions. Creating an array of evenly spaced values: Use np.linspace to generate an array with a specified number of points between two values:

np.linspace(début, fin_inclu, nombre_de_points)

Example:

np.linspace(0, 10, 5) # renvoie : array([0., 2.5, 5., 7.5, 10.])

Creating an array with a fixed step size: Use np.arange to generate an array with a fixed step between two values:

np.arange(début, fin exclu, pas)

Example:

np.arange(0, 10, 2) # renvoie : array([0, 2, 4, 6, 8])

Using numpy to calculate a derivative

To calculate the derivative of a curve, you can use np.gradient(), provided by the numpy module. This function calculates a numerical approximation to the derivative by evaluating differences between neighbouring array values:

np.gradient(y, x) # dérivée de y par rapport aux abscisses x

Specify the x coordinates to account for their spacing. Example:

import numpy as np
x = np.linspace(0, 10, 100) # génère 100 points entre 0 et 10
y = x**2 # fonction y = x²
dy_dx = np.gradient(y, x) # calcul de la dérivée dy/dx

Creating a scatter plot with Matplotlib. To display experimental or simulated data, a scatter plot is often more appropriate than a continuous line. You can use plt.scatter() from the Matplotlib module:

plt.scatter(x ,y, paramètres_graphiques) # paramètres graphiques :

color (or c) sets the plot colour; marker specifies the marker shape. Some options are: plus ‘+’, circle ‘o’, cross ‘x’, square ‘s’, triangle ‘v’, star ‘*’, point ‘.’; s specifies marker area in squared typographic points. Example:

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
x = np.linspace(0, 10, 20) # génère 20 points
y = x**2 # fonction y = x²
plt.scatter(x, y, color='blue', marker='o', s=50)
plt.title('Nuage de points')# ajout d'un titre
plt.xlim([0,10]) # limite de l'axe x
plt.ylim([0,100]) # limite de l'axe y
plt.xlabel('x') # nom de l'axe x
plt.ylabel('y') # nom de l'axe y
plt.show()

Instructions:

1. Model the theoretical data points for the titration curve pH = f(VB).

👉 To do this:

• Define an array of added volumes between 0.1 and 20 mL, with a step of 0.1 mL.

• Define the analytical concentrations during the titration:

CA,t = CA,0 × VA / (VA + VB)

CB,t = CB,0 × VB / (VA + VB)

• Calculate the extent of reaction per unit volume by solving the quadratic equation:

ξ2 – (CA,t + CB,t + KE/KA)ξ + CA,t × CB,t = 0

The value of ξ is then calculated as follows: ξ = (−b − √Δ) / (2a)

• Deduce the pH value.

2. Calculate the first derivative of the curve pH = f(VB).

3. Plot the modelled curve and its first derivative.

👉 To do this:

• Show the data points on the graph using triangular markers.

• Set the axis limits: x axis: [0,20] mL and y axis: [0,14] pH units.

• Add axis labels, a graph title and a legend.

B/ Finding and displaying the equivalence volume

The equivalence volume can be determined using the derivative method: the maximum of the derivative of the titration curve identifies the equivalence volume.

Finding extrema in an ndarray.

One advantage of the NumPy module is how easily it handles data arrays (ndarrays). Use the following functions to find extrema and their positions:

np.max(ndarray) ou np.min(ndarray) # renvoie la valeur maximale

This returns the maximum or minimum value in an array.

np.argmax(ndarray) ou np.argmin(ndarray) # renvoie l’indice de la

This returns the index of the maximum or minimum value. Once the equivalence volume has been identified, you can display the corresponding points on the graph:

plt.vlines(x, ymin, ymax, paramètres) # pour tracer une ligne

This draws a vertical line.

plt.hlines(y, xmin, xmax, paramètres) # pour tracer une ligne

This draws a horizontal line.

Instructions:

1. Determine the coordinates of the equivalence point and display them in the console.

👉 To do this:

• Find the index of the maximum of the derivative, then find the values of VB and pH at that position.

2. Show the coordinates of the equivalence point on the curve.

title: Exercise 2: Investigating Ostwald’s dilution law
body:
The degree of dissociation of a weak acid in water depends on its concentration: the more dilute the acid, the greater the degree of dissociation. We will demonstrate this law, known as Ostwald’s dilution law, for a formic acid solution with a concentration between 10-1 and 10-8 mol·L-1.

Given: Acid dissociation constant: KA = 10-3.75

Instructions:

1. Plot the degree of dissociation as a function of concentration.

👉 To do this:

• Generate an array of 10 000 initial concentration values ranging from 10-1 to 10-8 mol/L.

• Calculate the degree of dissociation from the extent of reaction per unit volume, obtained by solving the quadratic equation.

• Plot the degree of dissociation as a function of concentration, using a logarithmic scale for the x axis with the command

plt.xscale('log')

• Add a title and axis labels to the graph. We will now determine the threshold concentrations:

• Above which the reaction proceeds only slightly (degree of dissociation below 10 %).

• Below which the reaction is effectively complete (degree of dissociation above 90 %). The values 10 % and 90 % do not necessarily occur exactly in the array, so you will need to define a variable that calculates the difference between the degrees of dissociation in the array and these target values.

Instructions:

1. Determine and display the threshold concentrations.

👉 To do this:

• Calculate the difference between the degrees of dissociation in the array and the target values (10 % and 90 %).

• Find the indices of the smallest differences to identify the threshold concentrations.

• Display the corresponding concentration and degree of dissociation values in the console.

2. Plot these characteristic points.
